rejection_reason: Intended feature; consequences are by design.
title: emergencyWithdraw decrements totalStaked without calling _updatePool, retroactively repricing the pre-withdrawal window at the new smaller denominator
asset_impact: Protocol over-emits rewards: forfeited accrual from an emergency-withdrawing staker is redistributed pro-rata to survivors at a re-priced rate, rather than staying with the protocol. Amplifies DEDUP-001 solvency gap.
attack_path:
1. Alice and Bob both stake at t=0, totalStaked=20.
2. Bob calls emergencyWithdraw at t=100. totalStaked drops to 10; lastRewardTime and accRewardPerShare unchanged (no _updatePool).
3. At t=200 Alice claims. _updatePool computes elapsed=200 * rewardRate and divides by current totalStaked=10, crediting Alice for the full [0,200] period at the post-withdrawal denominator.
4. Alice receives ~200R instead of the fair 150R; Bob's forfeited 50R is redirected to Alice rather than retained by the protocol.
likelihood: medium - requires at least one emergencyWithdraw and no intervening _updatePool between that withdrawal and the next settlement. Normal in pools with sparse activity.
assumptions: A user triggers emergencyWithdraw while pool has other active stakers and _updatePool has not been called in the current block.
justification: Protocol-function impact (over-emission beyond nominal rewardRate) with stated assumptions; value leak to survivors. Not direct theft — the surviving staker did not steal, they received over-credited emissions the protocol should have retained. Matches C4 Medium.
